socra.com.Title: AI Platform Testing
socra.com.Description:
As a Beta Tester and UAT Specialist for the Socra AI platform, I executed exploratory testing to evaluate the product's quality and user experience. 
Without formal requirements, I acted as a real user, creatively navigating the platform to uncover bugs, identify usability issues,
 and assess its overall readiness for launch. This approach allowed me to discover critical defects and provide valuable,
 user-centric feedback that directly influenced the final product.
Responsibilities: Identified and documented a wide range of defects, from critical crashes to minor usability issues, using screen captures and detailed steps to reproduce.
Assessed the user flow and intuitiveness of the AI platform from an end-user perspective, providing actionable feedback to the development and design teams.
Contributed to the overall quality and stability of the product by proactively testing new features and their interactions with existing functionalities.
Provided qualitative feedback on the platform's performance, stability, and reliability under various real-world usage scenarios.

Agile Travel.Title: Travel e-commerce site
Agile Travel.Description: For the Agile Travel (Demonstration Project), I performed manual exploratory testing to evaluate the web application’s quality and functionality.I systematically explored the application to uncover bugs and design flaws, which I then formally documented into detailed test cases and bug reports.My work demonstrated my proficiency in both creative defect discovery and structured documentation, providing a clear record of my testing process and contributions to the project's quality in a professional setting.
Responsibilities: Conducted manual exploratory testing across the Agile Travel application to uncover bugs and potential user experience flaws.
Authored test cases based on exploratory findings, creating a structured and reusable test suite.
Documented and reported all discovered defects in a bug-tracking system, including steps to reproduce, expected vs. actual results, and supporting screenshots.
Assessed the application's overall functionality and usability to ensure a high-quality user experience.

uTest Rolex.Title: uTest Project: Rollex Application
uTest Rolex.Description: As a freelance QA Tester on the uTest platform, I contributed to the quality assurance of the Rollex application. My responsibilities included executing test cases and reporting bugs based on a client's specific requirements.Due to the confidential nature of this project, specific test cases and bug report details cannot be shared.This experience showcased my ability to work within a professional testing environment, adhere to client-defined test scenarios,and provide high-quality, actionable bug reports while respecting client confidentiality
Responsibilities: Executed pre-defined test cases to verify the functionality and usability of the Rollex application.
Documented and submitted professional-grade bug reports, adhering to the client’s and uTest’s quality standards.
Collaborated effectively with the uTest community and project managers, ensuring a clear and efficient communication of findings.
Adhered to project-specific Non-Disclosure Agreements (NDAs) by maintaining the confidentiality of all test data and project information.
Demonstrated a strong attention to detail and a commitment to quality in a professional, crowdsourced testing environment.

Sweet Shop.Title: Web Application
Sweet Shop.Description: On the Sweet Shop project, an internationally broken web application, I performed comprehensive exploratory and manual testing to identify and document defects. My primary focus was to evaluate the site's functionality from an end-user perspective, with particular attention given to the payment processing functionality.  This experience allowed me to practice my skills in discovering common real-world web application issues, including those related to forms, e-commerce transactions,and user flow.
Responsibilities: Conducted in-depth manual and exploratory testing across the Sweet Shop web application to uncover pre-existing bugs and usability issues.
Focused testing efforts on the payment processing and e-commerce functionalities, identifying critical defects in the checkout flow
Documented bugs and provided clear, concise reports detailing the nature of the issue, steps to reproduce, and expected versus actual results.
Analyzed the web application from a user's perspective, providing feedback on inconsistencies and areas for improvement in the user interface and user experience.

File Organizer.Title: Tool: File Organizer
File Organizer.Description: A robust command-line utility designed to solve the problem of digital clutter. The application scans a target directory and automatically categorizes files into a structured hierarchy based on File Type (Images, Documents, Installers, Videos) and Creation Date (Year/Month). It features intelligent conflict resolution to handle duplicate filenames without data loss and utilizes a Separation of Concerns architecture to ensure business logic is isolated from file system operations.
Responsibilities: I engineered the automated testing strategy using NUnit.
Implementing Data-Driven Testing to efficiently validate sorting logic across dozens of file types with minimal code.
I focused heavily on Negative Testing and Edge Case analysis.
Identifying and resolving critical stability issues (such as null pointer exceptions) to ensure the application handles invalid inputs safely without crashing.

Georgia E Antoniou Portfolio.Title: Personal Website, Portfolio
Georgia E Antoniou Portfolio.Description: This is my personal software testing portfolio, built with Blazor WebAssembly and hosted on GitHub Pages. It showcases my approach to test planning, positive and negative test case design, and thorough exploration of real user journeys. The site evolves as I experiment with new testing tools, techniques, and real-world scenarios.
Responsibilities: Designed the test plan for my Blazor portfolio site, clearly defining scope, test objectives, and priorities.
Created and documented detailed positive and negative test cases for all main pages (Home, Portfolio, About, Blog, Contact).
Executed cross-browser and responsive testing to verify the site behaves correctly on different devices and screen sizes.
Focused on functional and negative testing to check how the site handles unexpected user actions, broken URLs, and layout edge cases.
Logged findings, refined test cases based on results, and updated the portfolio content to fix usability or consistency issues.

Nick Polyderopoulos Portfolio.Title: Automated Testing Suite (C#, Playwright, NUnit)
Nick Polyderopoulos Portfolio.Description: Developed a robust automated regression suite for a professional portfolio site using Playwright and C#. The project focuses on ensuring UI stability, theme consistency, and responsive navigation through advanced element interactions and automated reporting.
Responsibilities: Automated UI Validation: Scripted automated tests to verify complex UI components, including theme toggling (Dark/Light mode) by asserting dynamic changes in CSS link attributes.
Advanced Interaction Testing: Developed logic to verify the functional state of expandable sections (Skills, Experiences) using attribute assertions and visibility checks.
State-Based Navigation Testing: Engineered tests for the Hamburger navigation menu by monitoring dynamic CSS class changes during sidebar transitions.
Automated Failure Reporting: Implemented a custom [TearDown] mechanism that automatically captures full-page screenshots and attaches them to NUnit test results upon failure for rapid debugging.
Stability Engineering: Optimized test reliability by replacing brittle XPaths with resilient user-facing locators and implementing auto-retrying assertions to handle asynchronous page renders.
